title: Deploy & Domain
summary: Deploy means creating a public link while keeping secrets in Environment Variables, not in code.

sections.heading: Orientation
sections.subtitle: Introduction to the Lesson
sections.contentMarkdown:
- **What will you learn?** **How to make your app accessible via a public link** — **and keep secrets safe**.
- **Why now?** **You have built an interface, a database, and AI** — **but it's still on localhost**. **No one else can use it**.
- **What after the lesson?** **You will distinguish between what is 'public' (link, name)** **and what is 'secret' (API keys)**.
bullets: **What will you learn?** **How to make your app accessible via a public link** — **and keep secrets safe**.

sections.heading: Tension
sections.subtitle: A good app, but stuck on your device
sections.contentMarkdown:
- **Everything works on `localhost`** — **but no one in the world can access it**.
- **You send `localhost:5173` to your friend** — **it won't open for them**. **The app is still just an idea on your device**.
- **Deploy** means **making it available on the internet**. **But the OpenAI key must remain secret** — **not in the code**.

sections.heading: Core idea
sections.subtitle: Public link + Protected secrets
sections.contentMarkdown:
- **Deploy** means **the code goes to a server** — **people access it from a public URL** (like `my-app.com`).
- **Secrets (API keys, database passwords)** **go to a 'vault' on the server** — **Environment Variables** — **not in GitHub**.
- **The difference:** **what people see (link, interface)** **versus what must remain hidden (keys)**.

sections.heading: Comparison
sections.subtitle: Key in code vs Key in vault
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Secret in code | Secret in Env Vars |
|-------------|----------------|
| **OpenAI key in a file on GitHub** — **anyone can see it and use it on your account**. **A financial and security disaster** | **The code is public — the keys are only in the server vault**. **The link is public, secrets are protected** |

sections.heading: Glossary
sections.subtitle: Two terms to start
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Term | Meaning | Example |
|---------|--------|------|
| **Deploy** | **Moving the app from your device to a server** — **a public URL that anyone can access** | **From localhost → `https://my-ai-app.com`** |
| **Environment Variables** | **A vault for secrets on the server** — **API keys and database passwords** | **OPENAI_API_KEY in Production settings** — **not in the code** |

sections.heading: Screenshot block (intent)
sections.contentMarkdown:
**Build log — Successful deployment:**

Every deploy = **a new version on the internet**. **The build log shows what succeeded and what failed** — **it's not a black box**.

sections.heading: Quiz
sections.subtitle: Quick confirmation
sections.contentMarkdown:
> **Quiz key:** correctIndex: 0

**Question:** **The app is running on your device. What is the most critical thing you might forget before deployment?**

**API keys in the Production vault** — **not in the code or GitHub**.
The color of the 'Submit' button in the interface.
The number of 404 pages.

**Explanation:** **Wrong secrets = the app crashes or gets stolen**. **The link is public — and secrets must stay in the vault**.

sections.heading: Mission
sections.subtitle: List: Public vs Secret
sections.contentMarkdown:
**Introduction:** **Before Deploy — distinguish what people see from what must remain hidden**. **10 minutes**.

**Submission:** **3 public items**, **3 secrets**, **which secret would be the most dangerous if leaked** and why.

**Evaluation criteria:**

| Dimension | Weight | Criteria |
|-------|-------|---------|
| Correct classification | 60% | **3 public (URL, interface, public content)**; **3 secrets (API keys, DB password, JWT secret)** |
| Risk priority | 40% | **Most dangerous secret due to logical reasons (money, user data, ...)** |
